chunk_map.heading: A file the team writes once steers every answer

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read
rules_evaluated.evidence: l8: 'A file written by all three of you' - closest; 'all three' resolves to product owner, designer, team lead named in the same sentence group; l6 'them' resolves to the list in the same sentence.
l4-8: no pointer at another file or slide; closest l4 'A file the agent reads each time' is a general claim, no positional callback.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no 'the X you did/saw' backward references

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read

rules_evaluated.evidence: l4-8: three paragraphs each carry a claim; closest to thin is l6 (a list of what to write down), still self-carrying under the header.
l1 header 'A file the team writes once steers every answer' vs l6 'write them down once' and l4 'shapes every answer after it'; closest l8 'steers better' stays within the header.

grep for Not X. Not Y. construction: none in l4-8; closest l8 triplet 'the product owner knows the outcome, the designer the customer's own words, the team lead what the agents may touch' carries three distinct concrete items, no empty leg; no superlatives, numbers or abstraction stacks.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide
rules_evaluated.evidence: view greps (banned words, ritual, leverage, the student) 0 hits; closest l8 'what the agents may touch' is plain engineering language, not repo dialect.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly
rules_evaluated.evidence: no bold on the slide (body l1-9); budget is <=1.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read
rules_evaluated.evidence: slide file inlined by include; single ## chunk with slide id l2, reaches the composed deck via the lecture manifest; no phase-less prose section.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js --file → OK, exit 0; no Phase/Step headers.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file → OK, no page-geometry pointers, exit 0.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no in-body links; view signals has_urls false and rule 13 is a review surface, no gate

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file → oversized: 0, exit 0; body is about 106 words in 3 paragraphs, 0 bullets.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing
rules_evaluated.evidence: l1 header is a claim 'A file the team writes once steers every answer' on a lecture slide, as the rule requires.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing
rules_evaluated.evidence: l6 closest to restating (the 'write them down once' list) but it adds the concrete content of the file; l8 adds the three-seat reason not stated in header or l4; no kicker, no design commentary.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header
rules_evaluated.evidence: single-slide file with no rename trace; l12 maintainer note records a rewrite from the Agents 101 slide, and the body answers the current header (once, steers every answer) with no inherited old-header bullets.

notes: Single-slide file; the one ## chunk is also chunk 0. Maintainer block carries one dated line (STATUS 2026-10-06), not an accept-note for any rule.
